title: Key poses: Gemini pixel pose + fixer (b) vs Gemini illustration pose -> E2 (c)
question: Can Gemini make on-model key poses (walk/run/jump/throw, rig H guides, SE) at the master's scale: directly as pixel art (b), or as an HD illustration then E2 pixelize (c, the untried 'key-pose illustration -> E2' idea)?
method: (b) refs illustration + m96 master x8 + guide -> fixer fix_sq -> lock2. (c) refs illustration + guide -> pz.py EC0 SE <h> --src. 2 samples per pose per route. Scale by head size (hair bbox = master 35 px, 'hn') or by rig guide height ('gh'). Identity = palette/material L1 and head ratio vs the master. Argon + Opus critics.
result: (c): all 8 illustrations on-model with good pose adherence. Head ratio at rig scale 1.17 +- 0.10 (consistently ~15% big), orphans 1.2%, E2 fidelity to its own source ssim_b .96-.98. (b): 2/8 came back as 3-figure sheets in a different chibi style. Head ratio 1.01 +- 0.22 (0.71-1.40), cleaner clusters (orphans 0.6%), palette closest to the master. Neither route is usable after only light cleanup.
verdict: Critics split: Opus says c (mean 5.0 vs 4.75; c's errors are local, b's are structural: hairstyle, eye style and proportions change per pose), Argon says b (cleaner blocks). Recommend (c) + head-matched scale + dark-cluster/outline cleanup + m96 head stamp.
